features.name: any_comment_uses_familiar_analogy
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment use an analogy to a familiar everyday scenario to make its point?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertions, uses an analogy that compares the issue under debate to a different, familiar/everyday scenario (e.g., comparing the issue to a common situation like driving, shopping, or cooking) to support its argument. Return 0 if no comment does. Merely quoting someone else's analogy without adopting it does not count; literal examples of the same issue, and hypotheticals that are not analogies to another scenario, do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence; generic delta-rule discussion is eligible. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

h0: any_comment_uses_familiar_analogy has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Discussions with any_comment_uses_familiar_analogy=1 have a higher probability of OP view change than those with 0.
note: Presence is assumed from "containing counter-arguments that use analogies". "Familiar scenario" is judged by the annotator without a fixed scale. OLS on binary outcome gives a linear probability model; association only. OC_comments may include outcome announcements, which the prompt excludes as evidence. Comment order and timing unknown.
